summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of recurrent UTIs and COPD, was admitted for treatment of a complicated urinary tract infection caused by cefepime-sensitive Klebsiella pneumoniae. She presented with urinary incontinence and had a history of frequent catheterization. IV cefepime was initiated via her existing PICC line, and her leukocytosis improved during the hospital stay. A chest CT revealed new right basilar consolidation, likely due to chronic aspiration given her neuromuscular impairment and patulous esophagus, but she remained afebrile and asymptomatic, so no additional treatment was initiated. She was managed for acute shoulder pain from a recent non-displaced scapular fracture with oxycodone and lidocaine patches. She was discharged home with services to complete a 7-day course of IV antibiotics, ongoing oxygen at 2L, and follow-up plans for pulmonary and swallow evaluation.
